description: A Dockerized Android emulator supporting multiple CPU architectures (x86 and arm64) with native performance and seamless ADB & Scrcpy Web access.

summary.one_liner: A Dockerized Android emulator that runs Android virtual devices in containers, with optional root/Magisk, PICO GApps, ARM app translation, and browser or ADB access.
summary.what_it_does: Runs an Android Virtual Device (Android 11 / API 30 per the README) inside a Docker container, started with docker compose up -d. A bundled scrcpy-web interface lets you view and control the device from a web browser, with H264, Tiny H264, and Broadway.js streaming options. The device is also reachable over ADB on port 5555 from the host or other networked machines, and desktop scrcpy can connect to it. Optional environment variables enable root with Magisk, PICO GApps, and ARM/ARM64 app translation via ndk_translation, and set RAM, screen resolution, density and a private DNS. First boot runs a setup script that can take 10-15 minutes, and logs from the emulator and boot process go to Docker's log system. Versioned Docker image tags are published from GitHub Releases.
use_cases: Run Android apps in a container for automated testing
Control an Android emulator from a web browser
Set up a headless Android device in CI pipelines
Install ARM-only Android apps on an x86 host
Share a remote Android emulator with a team
Connect to an emulator with adb or desktop scrcpy
notable: Browser-based device control through an integrated scrcpy-web interface
ARM/ARM64 app support on x86_64 via ndk_translation, enabled by an environment variable
Optional root with Magisk and PICO GApps, set at first boot
Multi-architecture support for x86 and arm64 hosts
Docker image tags generated from GitHub Releases plus edge builds from main
caveats: Requires KVM hardware virtualization (vmx or svm CPU flag, /dev/kvm access)
First boot takes about 10-15 minutes, longer with root or ARM translation enabled
ROOT_SETUP, GAPPS_SETUP and ARM_TRANSLATION cannot be undone without recreating the data volume
Only Android 30 (Android 11) is currently supported, per the roadmap
